pr_title: Display localised names for system folders
pr_comments: @duke7553 could we put this in the `LoadExtendedItemProperties` method? It won't hurt performance, only issue is that it will briefly show the untranslated name (maybe acceptable)
@gave92 Actually we can do this from the Win32 component. That's what a tried first.
@Jaiganeshkumaran that would be pretty slow as well I think
@gave92 What should I do then? SHGetLocalizedName is not available for UWP apps.
@Jaiganeshkumaran I think the current method (StorageFolder) is good, and performance issues can be solved by moving this to the LoadExtendedItemProperties() method
@gave92 But then it will not be shown in the folder list.
We can have it as a optional feature
@gave92 Since the name is shown on the files list rather than something like the properties, I'm not going to put this in extended properties. Instead we can have it as an option feature.
@Jaiganeshkumaran if you put this in LoadExtendedItemProperties the translated name *will* be shown on the file list. That method has nothing to do with the properties window
@gave92 But what's the difference? It's used currently for stuff in properties window right?

Here's an issue with localization. In English (United States) it's 'localized' but in other regions it is 'localised'. I've added a resource file for en-gb however it will use the en-us version even if it's set to some other en other than en-us or en-uk because Windows provides many en regions. Should I add resource files for each one of en region using MAT?

@Jaiganeshkumaran nope, it's called from GenericFileBrowser and GridViewBrowser to load some file info (e.g. file thumbnail, OneDrive sync status, etc)
It's used to delay loading of "slow" file properties to improve performance, it should be a good place to get the localized name as well.
@gave92 But now the names appear after the page has fully loaded which makes it look bad.

@Jaiganeshkumaran yeah I don't particularly mind that (better than no translated name and better than slow file list loading) but I understand your concern.
@duke7553 do you have any thoughts on this?
@Jaiganeshkumaran yes this is the cause of that issue as well. I know it's not ideal but does not degrade performance.

> We can have it as a optional feature

@Jaiganeshkumaran We should not add an optional feature in this case since it will slow down the app for users who turn it on who might not be aware of the side affects.
@yaichenbaum Then can I close this pull request?

> @yaichenbaum Then can I close this pull request?

We would love to include this if you can find a way to implement it without any side effects.

issue_context.title: Show localised (localized) names for system folders
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Not really. In File Explorer, it will show the localized name instead of the real name for system folders such as Users folder.

![2020-06-25 11-13-34_Trim](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/45227503/85666622-4e3d7e00-b6da-11ea-8c21-dfb1d3e0977b.gif)

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Files UWP should show to localized name instead of the real name for system folders.
comments: @yaichenbaum Could you assign me on this issue?
@Jaiganeshkumaran Are you still planning to work on this issue?
@yaichenbaum Yes but only if you let me use StorageFolder

@Jaiganeshkumaran The reason we don't use StorageFolder over there is because it will slow down the loading of the items. Perhaps there is another way to find the localized name without using StorageFolder.
@yaichenbaum There's a function named SHGetLocalizedName but it's not allowed in UWP. SHGetFileInfo can also be used but it is also not allowed.

> @yaichenbaum There's a function named SHGetLocalizedName but it's not allowed in UWP. SHGetFileInfo can also be used but it is also not allowed.

We can probably put that in the FullTrustProcess.

review_comments: Here you could fill the name field with the untranslated name (findata.cFileName) in both cases. It will automatically update once the LoadExtendedItemProperties completes. Might look much better that an empty name.
Here the translated name is already available -> folder.DisplayName
